Currently onsite are one 7.2 mgd conventional tertiary sand filter (DynaSand), two 5.5 mgd conventional tertiary cloth filters (AquaDisk), 10 percolation ponds which vary in size, five banks of UV disinfection, 18 containment wells and 13 relief wells.

The RIX treatment process utilizes in-situ native soil filtration by applying the secondary treated wastewater to a series of shallow earthen basins on a rotational basis so that basins can be operated on alternately wet and dry cycles. As the secondary effluent percolates through the unsaturated soil media to the groundwater table, physical, biological and chemical processes take place within the soil structure.

The extracted groundwater, together with the filtered water from the conventional tertiary filters (Dynasand and AquaDisk), is then channeled to flow through UV disinfection banks prior to discharging to the Santa Ana River, Reach 4.
